summary: This note surveys the farm-to-table movement in late 2023, walking through seasonal salad ingredients from September to December, including root vegetables, orchard fruits, winter greens and herbs. It collects tips and recipes from farmers, chefs and gardeners, covers richer cool-season dressings, and ends on mindful eating and farmer-chef collaboration as a commitment to communities and the planet.
one_line: A guide to fall and winter farm-to-table salads and dressings in 2023, with expert tips on seasonal produce, herbs and mindful eating.
key_facts: Sarah McIntire, a farm-owner from Oregon, says autumn brings pumpkins, beets, kale and heirloom carrots in place of summer squash and berries.

Chef Daniel Houghton of the 'Green Leaf Bistro' in Vermont suggests a Shaved Root Vegetable Salad: slice beets, carrots and radishes thinly with a mandoline, toss with a tangy mustard dressing, and add toasted walnuts.
Root vegetables take center stage in October and can be shaved, spiralized or thinly sliced for crunch in salads.
Lisa Tremont, farm-to-table advocate and cookbook author, shared 'Autumn's Apple Walnut Salad' with sliced apples, walnuts, blue cheese and a balsamic reduction.
Apples and pears from the November late harvest add sweetness to salads, and apple sweetness complements bitter greens like radicchio or arugula.
Hardy greens like kale, chard and spinach withstand the cold in December and become sweeter after a frost.
Heather Morris, an urban gardener from Seattle, recommends massaging kale with olive oil and salt to soften it and bring out its complex flavors.
Herbs such as sage, rosemary, thyme and parsley can elevate fall salads, and gardener James Fielding says growing your own is cost-effective and gives the freshest flavors.
On October 10th, 2023, culinary blogger Maria Gonzalez demonstrated seasonal dressings on her YouTube channel using pomegranate molasses and pumpkin seed oil.
Cooler-month dressings get richer, such as creamy tahini dressing and zesty ginger soy vinaigrette.
Nutritionist David Bright hosts a mindful eating workshop by December encouraging people to savor each bite.
Chef Amelia Fortes and farmer Greg Nicholson debuted a 'Root-to-Leaf' meal concept on September 9th where nothing goes to waste.
A suggested pairing for a seasonal salad is fresh apple with goat cheese and toasted pumpkin seeds.
